overview: Black answers 1.Nf3 with a developing knight move that does not stake a claim to the centre. White usually plays 2.d4 or 2.e4 and gets a comfortable space edge, or transposes into a Chigorin Defence-like position with ...d5 and ...Nc6. Black aims for a solid development and decent play, but has no theory to rely on.

white_ideas.idea: Take the centre with d4 and e4 and develop naturally

black_ideas.idea: Develop ...e5 or ...d5 and meet central expansion with solid pawn moves

typical_structures.structure: Varies; usually transposes to d4 or e4 games with Black's knight early on c6

character.notes: Not enough theory to say; I would expect quiet, transposing play.

soundness.notes: Playable but gives White an easy centre; not refuted.

structure.notes: Depends on the transposition; centre undecided.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly ever play 1...Nc6 against 1.Nf3.

level.notes: Transposition knowledge more than memory; intermediate by default.

character.reason: Unfamiliar line; reasoning from the moves it looks quiet and transposing.

level.reason: Nothing to memorise but plans need understanding.
